title: A Comprehensive Review of YOLO Architectures in Computer Vision: From YOLOv1 to YOLOv8 and YOLO-NAS
venue: Machine Learning and Knowledge Extraction (MDPI), Vol. 5, No. 4
abstract: This paper traces the evolution of YOLO across all major versions up to YOLOv8 and YOLO-NAS, covering architectural changes, training methodologies, standard evaluation metrics, and postprocessing approaches. It synthesizes key developmental insights and proposes future research directions for advancing real-time detection capabilities across robotics, autonomous vehicles, and surveillance applications.
relevance_note: Canonical reference for understanding all YOLO variants being evaluated as the team baseline, including YOLOv8 and YOLO-NAS performance characteristics.

title: Benchmarking Deep Learning Models for Object Detection on Edge Computing Devices
abstract: The authors evaluate YOLOv8 (Nano, Small, Medium), EfficientDet Lite variants, and SSD across Raspberry Pi variants and Jetson Orin Nano devices, measuring inference latency, power consumption, and mean Average Precision. They find that lower mAP models such as SSD MobileNet V1 are more energy-efficient and faster, while YOLOv8 Medium demands more resources; TPU accelerators improve performance, and INT8 quantization reduces latency on the Jetson Orin Nano to as low as 23 ms for YOLOv8n.
relevance_note: Directly benchmarks YOLOv8 on Jetson Orin Nano with latency/power metrics, which maps precisely to the team's target hardware.

title: A Performance Analysis of You Only Look Once Models for Deployment on Constrained Computational Edge Devices in Drone Applications
abstract: The paper investigates deploying YOLOv8n and YOLOv8s on Jetson Orin Nano, Orin NX, and Raspberry Pi 5 for drone computer vision, evaluating detection accuracy, inference speed, and energy consumption with post-training quantization. YOLOv8n achieves 52 FPS on Jetson Orin NX and 65 FPS with INT8 quantization via TensorRT. The Raspberry Pi 5 failed to meet real-time requirements. The study identifies latency trade-offs between edge and cloud processing architectures.
relevance_note: Provides detailed FPS and latency numbers for YOLOv8 variants on Jetson Orin Nano/NX at the 20–65 FPS range relevant to the <50 ms obstacle detection requirement.

title: YOLOv9: Learning What You Want to Learn Using Programmable Gradient Information
abstract: YOLOv9 addresses information loss in deep neural networks through Programmable Gradient Information (PGI), which preserves complete input information for the target task. It also introduces the Generalized Efficient Layer Aggregation Network (GELAN) based on gradient path planning. Validated on MS COCO, models trained from scratch with GELAN+PGI achieve competitive results versus large pre-trained models while using conventional convolution operators for better parameter efficiency.
relevance_note: YOLOv9 is one of the YOLO variants to benchmark against the team's YOLOv8 baseline for accuracy-speed trade-offs on edge hardware.

title: YOLOv10: Real-Time End-to-End Object Detection
abstract: YOLOv10 eliminates reliance on non-maximum suppression (NMS) post-processing using consistent dual assignments for NMS-free training, and introduces an efficiency-accuracy driven model design strategy. YOLOv10-S is 1.8x faster than RT-DETR-R18 under similar AP on COCO, and YOLOv10-B achieves 46% less latency and 25% fewer parameters than YOLOv9-C at equivalent performance.
relevance_note: NMS-free design reduces end-to-end inference latency, directly helping meet the team's <50 ms obstacle detection target on Jetson hardware.

title: DETRs Beat YOLOs on Real-time Object Detection
venue: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR) 2024
abstract: RT-DETR is the first real-time end-to-end object detector that uses an efficient hybrid encoder for multi-scale feature processing and uncertainty-minimal query selection to enhance accuracy. It achieves 53.1–54.3% AP on COCO at 74–108 FPS on a T4 GPU, surpassing comparable YOLO variants while offering flexible speed adjustments without retraining.
relevance_note: RT-DETR offers an alternative transformer-based architecture to YOLO with competitive latency, relevant when evaluating detection backbones for the wheelchair perception pipeline.

title: ByteTrack: Multi-Object Tracking by Associating Every Detection Box
abstract: ByteTrack associates every detection box (including low-confidence ones) with existing tracklets, rather than discarding low-score detections. By leveraging similarities between low-confidence detections and tracklets to recover true objects and filter background, it achieves 80.3 MOTA, 77.3 IDF1, and 63.1 HOTA on MOT17 at 30 FPS on a V100 GPU. It yields consistent improvement across 9 state-of-the-art trackers.
relevance_note: ByteTrack is the most widely deployed MOT algorithm pairable with YOLO for person tracking in the wheelchair perception pipeline due to its speed and robustness.

title: Observation-Centric SORT: Rethinking SORT for Robust Multi-Object Tracking
venue: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR) 2023
abstract: OC-SORT addresses limitations of Kalman filter-based MOT during occlusions and non-linear motion by using an observation-centric approach. Instead of linear state predictions, it computes a virtual trajectory over occlusion periods from detector measurements to fix error accumulation. OC-SORT achieves real-time performance at 700+ FPS on a single CPU and sets state-of-the-art on MOT17, MOT20, KITTI, and DanceTrack.
relevance_note: OC-SORT's robustness to occlusion and non-linear motion is critical for tracking pedestrians in indoor wheelchair navigation where people frequently duck behind furniture.

title: StrongSORT: Make DeepSORT Great Again
abstract: StrongSORT significantly improves DeepSORT across object detection, feature embedding, and trajectory association. It introduces AFLink (appearance-free global association without appearance information) and GSI (Gaussian-smoothed interpolation to handle missing detections). StrongSORT++ achieves state-of-the-art on MOT17, MOT20, DanceTrack, and KITTI with minimal computational overhead.
relevance_note: StrongSORT offers high identity accuracy via re-identification features, useful for maintaining consistent person IDs in crowded indoor corridors near a wheelchair.

title: BoT-SORT: Robust Associations Multi-Pedestrian Tracking
abstract: BoT-SORT is a robust multi-object tracking system that merges motion and appearance information along with camera-motion compensation and a more accurate Kalman filter state vector. The BoT-SORT tracker ranked first on MOTChallenge benchmarks for both MOT17 and MOT20 in MOTA, IDF1, and HOTA metrics, achieving 80.5 MOTA, 80.2 IDF1, and 65.0 HOTA on MOT17.
relevance_note: BoT-SORT's camera-motion compensation is beneficial for a wheelchair-mounted camera that may move unpredictably, improving tracker stability.

title: Simple Online and Realtime Tracking with a Deep Association Metric
venue: IEEE International Conference on Image Processing (ICIP) 2017
abstract: DeepSORT extends SORT with visual appearance information using a deep association metric learned on large-scale person re-identification data. During online application, associations are established using nearest neighbor queries in visual appearance space. The extensions reduce identity switches by 45% over SORT while maintaining competitive performance at high frame rates.
relevance_note: DeepSORT is the foundational tracker from which StrongSORT and others derive; understanding it is essential for selecting and tuning the team's tracking stack.

title: HopTrack: A Real-time Multi-Object Tracking System for Embedded Devices
abstract: HopTrack is a real-time multi-object tracking system designed for embedded devices, using a novel discretized static and dynamic matching approach and a content-aware dynamic sampling technique. On Jetson AGX Xavier, it achieves 39.29 FPS with 63.12% MOTA on MOT16, while reducing energy consumption by 20.8%, power draw by 5%, and memory usage by 8%. The framework is detector-agnostic.
relevance_note: HopTrack directly targets embedded GPUs in the Jetson family and achieves 24+ FPS under resource contention, making it a strong candidate for the wheelchair's Orin Nano.

title: Onboard Dynamic-Object Detection and Tracking for Autonomous Robot Navigation with RGB-D Camera
venue: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (RA-L), Vol. 9, No. 1, pp. 651-658
abstract: A lightweight detection and tracking system for small robots in crowded environments uses an RGB-D camera with a novel ensemble detection strategy combining multiple computationally efficient but low-accuracy detectors to achieve real-time high-accuracy obstacle detection. The system achieves 0.11 m position error and 0.23 m/s velocity error when tested on a quadcopter's onboard computer, and is released as an open-source ROS package.
relevance_note: Demonstrates a complete onboard RGB-D detection+tracking stack on resource-constrained hardware running ROS, directly analogous to the wheelchair's Jetson+RealSense setup.

title: A Real-Time Dynamic Obstacle Tracking and Mapping System for UAV Navigation and Collision Avoidance with an RGB-D Camera
venue: IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA) 2023
abstract: A real-time system for UAVs equipped with RGB-D cameras (Intel RealSense D435i) to perceive and avoid obstacles in crowded environments combines occupancy voxel mapping for identifying dynamic obstacles, Kalman and continuity filters for tracking, and Markov chain-based trajectory prediction. It distinguishes stationary from moving obstacles and is computationally efficient for resource-constrained UAVs, released as an open-source ROS package.
relevance_note: ICRA paper using Intel RealSense for real-time dynamic obstacle tracking in constrained environments, directly transferable to the wheelchair navigation context.

title: Autonomous Navigation in Dynamic Human Environments with an Embedded 2D LiDAR-based Person Tracker
abstract: This paper presents a real-time tracking system combining a 2D LiDAR-based human detection network and an efficient multi-object tracker, integrated with navigation planning on a quadruped robot. The system achieves 85.45% average MOTA while running at 20 Hz on an NVIDIA Jetson Xavier NX platform, validated in real-world experiments showing how accurate person tracking enhances collision avoidance in shared environments.
relevance_note: Demonstrates a complete 2D LiDAR person tracking pipeline running at 20 Hz on Jetson Xavier NX in real-world dynamic indoor environments — directly analogous to the wheelchair use case.

title: DR-SPAAM: A Spatial-Attention and Auto-regressive Model for Person Detection in 2D Range Data
venue: IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS) 2020
abstract: DR-SPAAM proposes a forward-looking paradigm for person detection in 2D LiDAR range data, keeping intermediate features from the backbone as a template and recurrently updating it as new scans arrive, avoiding expensive multi-scan alignment. It achieves state-of-the-art results on the DROW dataset at 87.2 FPS on a laptop GPU and 22.6 FPS on an embedded GPU, with a PyTorch implementation and pre-trained models released.
relevance_note: Efficient person detection directly from 2D LiDAR at ~22 FPS on embedded GPU, making it viable for the wheelchair's LiDAR-based person detection layer.

title: DROW: Real-Time Deep Learning based Wheelchair Detection in 2D Range Data
venue: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (RA-L) / ICRA 2017
abstract: DROW is a CNN-based detector for identifying wheelchairs and walkers in 2D laser range data, using a depth preprocessing step and a voting scheme that significantly improves CNN performance. Evaluated on a dataset of 464,000 laser scans with 24,000 annotated examples, achieving state-of-the-art detection results, with a ROS implementation released. The approach generalizes beyond wheelchairs to other objects in 2D range data.
relevance_note: Foundational work for wheelchair/person detection in 2D LiDAR, directly relevant since the team's platform is a wheelchair using a 2D LiDAR.

title: Depth Anything: Unleashing the Power of Large-Scale Unlabeled Data
venue: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR) 2024
abstract: Depth Anything is a practical foundation model for monocular depth estimation that scales up training by designing a data engine to collect and annotate ~62M unlabeled images. It employs data augmentation to create challenging optimization targets and auxiliary supervision to transfer semantic knowledge from pre-trained encoders. The model achieves strong zero-shot performance and state-of-the-art results when fine-tuned with metric depth data from NYUv2 and KITTI.
relevance_note: Provides a pre-trained monocular depth model deployable via TensorRT on Jetson for depth-informed obstacle detection when RealSense depth is unavailable or noisy.

title: Depth Anything V2
abstract: Depth Anything V2 improves over V1 through three strategies: replacing all labeled real images with synthetic images, scaling up the capacity of the teacher model, and teaching student models via large-scale pseudo-labeled real images. The resulting models are over 10x faster than competing diffusion-based approaches while achieving superior accuracy, with model sizes from 25M to 1.3B parameters and a versatile evaluation benchmark.
relevance_note: V2's lightweight variants are deployable on Jetson Orin Nano for supplementary depth estimation to complement the RealSense in regions with reflective surfaces.

title: Real-time Monocular Depth Estimation on Embedded Systems
venue: IEEE International Conference on Image Processing (ICIP) 2024
abstract: The paper proposes RT-MonoDepth and RT-MonoDepth-S, two lightweight neural network models for monocular depth estimation balancing computational efficiency with accuracy. On Jetson Nano, the models achieve 18–31 FPS; on Jetson AGX Orin, 253–364 FPS at 640x192 resolution. They deliver accuracy comparable to prior depth estimation methods while executing substantially faster than existing lightweight alternatives on the KITTI dataset.
relevance_note: RT-MonoDepth-S achieves 364 FPS on Jetson AGX Orin and ~31 FPS on Jetson Nano, suggesting feasible deployment on the Orin Nano for real-time depth at low compute cost.

title: Efficient Obstacle Detection and Tracking Using RGB-D Sensor Data in Dynamic Environments for Robotic Applications
abstract: This paper employs a u-depth map for obstacle detection with dynamic thresholding on depth images, introduces a restricted v-depth map technique for improved dimension estimation, and presents a new algorithm to track obstacles until they leave the field of view. Testing across multiple datasets shows the method outperforms vision-based state-of-the-art methods in state estimation of dynamic obstacles and execution time.
relevance_note: Provides a lightweight depth-image-based obstacle detection and tracking method applicable to the RealSense-equipped wheelchair without requiring heavy 3D point cloud processing.

title: Dynamic Occupancy Grid Map with Semantic Information Using Deep Learning-Based BEVFusion Method with Camera and LiDAR Fusion
abstract: This paper integrates camera and LiDAR data through BEVFusion in bird's-eye view format to create dynamic occupancy grid maps with semantic object classification (vehicles, bicycles, pedestrians) alongside position and velocity information, using Dempster-Shafer evidence theory to manage occupancy probabilities. Testing on nuScenes shows that an edge-based update approach reduces directional errors by 37% during turning maneuvers.
relevance_note: BEVFusion-based LiDAR+camera semantic occupancy grids provide a costmap approach for the wheelchair's ROS2 Nav2 local planner with dynamic obstacle awareness.

title: JRDB: A Dataset and Benchmark of Egocentric Robot Visual Perception of Humans in Built Environments
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence (TPAMI)
abstract: JRDB is an egocentric dataset collected from JackRabbot, a social mobile manipulator, comprising 64 minutes of annotated multimodal sensor data including 360° stereo RGB video, 3D point clouds from multiple lidar systems, audio, RGB-D footage, and fisheye imagery. It features 2.3 million bounding boxes and 1.8 million 3D cuboids across over 3,500 human trajectories in indoor and outdoor environments, with benchmarks and metrics for person detection and tracking.
relevance_note: JRDB provides robot-perspective person detection and tracking data at low sensor heights in indoor environments, making it the most directly applicable benchmark dataset for this project.

title: A Comparative Study of 3D Person Detection: Sensor Modalities and Robustness in Diverse Indoor and Outdoor Environments
venue: International Conference on Computer Vision Theory and Applications (VISAPP) 2026
abstract: This study evaluates camera-only (BEVDepth), LiDAR-only (PointPillars), and fusion-based (DAL) 3D person detection approaches using the JRDB dataset across varying occlusion and distance levels in indoor and outdoor scenes. Fusion models provide superior results in challenging conditions, though DAL remains sensitive to sensor misalignment and LiDAR-based corruptions. The camera-based approach showed weakest performance under occlusion.
relevance_note: Provides a direct comparison of sensor modality choices (camera vs LiDAR vs fusion) for robot-viewpoint indoor person detection, directly informing the wheelchair team's sensor fusion design.

title: From the Desks of ROS Maintainers: A Survey of Modern & Capable Mobile Robotics Algorithms in the Robot Operating System 2
abstract: Written by key ROS Navigation maintainers, this survey examines the state of robotic navigation in ROS 2, covering new systems without parallel in ROS 1 and discussing both contemporary research and established methods across various robot types. It covers Nav2 planners (Hybrid A*, Smac, MPPI), costmap layers, SLAM integration, and addresses dynamic environments, along with implementations not yet documented in academic literature.
relevance_note: Authoritative reference for the ROS2/Nav2 perception and navigation stack that the wheelchair will likely use, covering costmap design, dynamic obstacles, and sensor integration.

title: Dynamic Object Removal for Effective SLAM
abstract: This paper proposes a two-phase methodology for improving SLAM performance in dynamic environments: first, identifying dynamic objects using flow-based detection, then applying video inpainting to eliminate them from scenes. Evaluated against ORB-SLAM2 and LSD baseline algorithms, the method does not require significant modifications to baseline SLAM algorithms while improving localization and motion planning through dynamic object removal.
relevance_note: Removing dynamic persons from the SLAM map is essential for maintaining a stable static map in the wheelchair's indoor environment, directly addressing a core pipeline challenge.

title: RGB-D-Inertial SLAM in Indoor Dynamic Environments with Long-term Large Occlusion
abstract: A visual-inertial SLAM approach for indoor dynamic environments combines dense and sparse feature processing to track camera movement, segment dynamic objects into clusters, and preserve a static environmental map, without requiring prior semantic information. The framework handles camera localization when dynamic objects create substantial visual blockages over extended periods, demonstrating competitive performance under prolonged, substantial occlusion.
relevance_note: Addresses the wheelchair scenario where pedestrians heavily occlude the camera view in narrow corridors, preventing localization failure.

title: From Detection to Action Recognition: An Edge-Based Pipeline for Robot Human Perception
abstract: A complete processing pipeline for mobile service robots integrates human detection, tracking, and action recognition, operating in near real-time while ensuring all stages run on the edge to minimize dependence on centralized servers. Various state-of-the-art models were tested for performance and efficiency, and evaluated on a custom household activity dataset, demonstrating applicability in healthcare and assisted living environments.
relevance_note: Provides a full edge-deployed human perception pipeline for assistive robots in healthcare settings, directly analogous to the wheelchair's need for onboard-only inference.

title: ForceFormer: Exploring Social Force and Transformer for Pedestrian Trajectory Prediction
abstract: ForceFormer integrates social forces into a Transformer-based stochastic generative model, using a driving force from the destination to simulate target guidance and repulsive forces to model avoidance among nearby pedestrians. The model matches state-of-the-art distance error performance while notably decreasing collisions, especially in dense pedestrian scenarios, on widely used pedestrian datasets.
relevance_note: Enables the wheelchair to predict pedestrian motion in crowded indoor spaces, allowing proactive obstacle avoidance rather than purely reactive braking.

title: Motion Planning in Dynamic Environments Using Context-Aware Human Trajectory Prediction
abstract: The research combines intention recognition with trajectory optimisation-based motion planning for mobile manipulators in dynamic environments. GPU-accelerated predicted composite distance fields reduce computation time. Validated on a Toyota Human Support Robot using live RGB-D sensor data and introducing the Oxford-IHM dataset for indoor human trajectory prediction with motion-capture tracking.
relevance_note: Demonstrates coupling trajectory prediction with motion planning for an indoor service robot using RGB-D data, analogous to the wheelchair's need for predictive collision avoidance.

title: Benchmarking Jetson Edge Devices with an End-to-End Video-Based Anomaly Detection System
venue: Future of Information and Communication Conference (FICC) 2024
abstract: Researchers deployed a video-based anomaly detection system across NVIDIA Jetson Nano, AGX Xavier, and Orin Nano, achieving 47.56 FPS inference speed on a Jetson edge device with only 3.11 GB RAM usage using TorchTensorRT optimization. The Jetson Orin Nano delivers 15% better performance than its predecessor while consuming 50% less energy.
relevance_note: End-to-end video pipeline benchmark on Jetson Orin Nano confirms real-time throughput feasibility and provides energy/RAM baselines for planning the wheelchair perception stack.

title: Panopticus: Omnidirectional 3D Object Detection on Resource-constrained Edge Devices
venue: ACM International Conference on Mobile Computing and Networking (MobiCom) 2024
abstract: Panopticus uses an adaptive multi-branch detection scheme that dynamically adjusts model architecture based on available hardware resources and spatial complexities for 360-degree 3D detection on edge devices. It improves accuracy by 62% on average given a strict 33 ms latency objective, and achieves 2.1x latency reduction compared to baselines. For Jetson Orin Nano (6.3 GB memory), large modules are detached to prevent memory overloading.
relevance_note: Panopticus demonstrates adaptive 3D detection within 33 ms latency on Jetson Orin Nano, providing a concrete architecture template for the wheelchair's real-time safety constraint.

title: YOLO-IHD: Improved Real-Time Human Detection System for Indoor Drones
abstract: YOLO-IHD adapts the YOLOv7 architecture for UAV-based indoor human detection with optimized convolutional layers, attention mechanisms, a small-object detection layer, CSPSPPF module, and the Mish activation function. The model achieves a 42.51% improvement in mAP@0.5 over baseline YOLOv7-tiny on the IHD dataset and a 33.05% improvement on VisDrone, with enhanced real-time capabilities on onboard drone computers.
relevance_note: Architecturally relevant as a YOLO variant tuned for small-object indoor human detection from non-canonical viewpoints (overhead from drones vs. low from wheelchair), both non-automotive scenarios.
